Buzz Aldrin (Edwin Aldrin) went down to the surface with Armstrong in the lunar module Eagle, and he became the second person to walk on the Moon [1][2]. The third crew member was Michael Collins, the command module pilot. He stayed in lunar orbit aboard Columbia while the other two were on the surface, then brought them home after they rejoined him [2][3]. The mission launched on 16 July 1969 and returned to Earth on 24 July 1969 [2].
